problems.status: Confirmed proof gap / false overbroad criterion
problems.claim: Condition(*) iff z is in F-(w) for pairwise totally linked sequences; same proof for later enlarged H domains
problems.check: Take distinct z_n=iota(1+1/n) on F-(w), limit iota(1) not w. Since g preserves the leaf, g^-k z_i TL z_j for all i,j,k. First clause of(*) fails while the claimed RHS holds.
problems.counterevidence: Distinct NC fixed-point sequences have restrictions preventing the generic common-leaf example; the initial restricted lemma is not disproved by this example.
problems.impact: Remark5.22 removes that restriction and its proof method is used for the enlarged-domain accumulation control in Proposition5.44; the claimed transfer argument lacks common-leaf cases.
problems.repair: Restrict the criterion and separately prove on-leaf, constant and mixed-subsequence cases at every extension stage.

independent_acceptance_check.reason: Definition4.1 explicitly includes same-leaf pairs. Distinct points on the negative leaf of w remain mutually totally linked under every inverse iterate, violating the first clause of (*) despite satisfying Corollary5.8. Observation5.6 has an off-leaf hypothesis absent from the corollary. Lemma5.21's distinct NC case is not refuted, but Remark5.22 extends its proof to the enlarged domain used by Proposition5.44; the invocation lacks its hypothesis. Off-leaf restriction alone does not certify the enlarged-domain repair.

problems.status: Confirmed invalid premise in sharpness proof
problems.claim: No reversing self-equivalence follows from an attractor but no repelling set on N'
problems.check: For a proper forward trapping U on compact closed N', its increasing basin union of phi_-nT U cannot cover N' by compactness and bijectivity. Complement is a nonempty dual repeller.
problems.counterevidence: An actual asymmetric closed Anosov flow may forbid reversal despite having both attractors and repellers; theorem existence statement not refuted.
problems.impact: The stated reason required for the final contradiction proving non-orbit-equivalence fails; classification result does not depend backwards on sharpness.
problems.repair: Construct and verify a different asymmetry, including compatibility with subsequent gluings.

independent_acceptance_check.reason: PDF49 explicitly uses an attracting set but no repelling set to preclude reversal of the closed N' made by gluing the two torus boundaries, and PDF50 uses this obstruction in the non-equivalence proof. A proper trapping U has basin union of increasing inverse time translates; compactness and invertibility preclude that union being the entire closed manifold, producing a nonempty dual repeller. A different verified asymmetry could work; the theorem itself is not refuted.

problems.claim: Independent coordinate translations and diagonal dilations give Anosov-like affine actions
problems.check: tau1 preserves every horizontal leaf but has no fixed point; tau2 acts trivially on first coordinate, also disproving claimed projection faithfulness.
problems.counterevidence: Correcting the algebraic-independence wording does not remove these generators.
problems.impact: Example and trivial-plane nonrigidity illustration fail; main rigidity theorem excludes trivial planes.
problems.repair: Use a coupled translation (1,1), faithful Laurent-polynomial module, and independent dilations. Report verifies all axioms, density, equal spectra and nonconjugacy.

independent_acceptance_check.reason: AxiomA1 requires a fixed point on a preserved leaf. The stated coordinate translations preserve horizontal/vertical leaves without fixed points. The coupled-translation replacement was checked analytically: algebraic independence gives faithful Laurent normal form, all nontrivial translations move both leaf spaces, q!=1 gives the required hyperbolicity, and the character recurrence proves density. Dense translations and common D_a force any equivariant homeomorphism to be identity, yielding the stated nonconjugacy. All six axioms checked; the core theorem excludes trivial planes.

problems.claim: Everywhere-hyperbolic dynamics proposed as a useful class
problems.check: Condition2 with K+=K-={x} forbids all convergent distinct-element sequences. Condition3 for {x,u}, u!=x, yields infinitely many distinct elements by injectivity, and hence just such a subsequence.
problems.counterevidence: This does not affect A1-A6 or main results.
problems.impact: Proposed class is empty as written.
problems.repair: Exclude degenerate compact sets and specify nondegenerate segments; adequacy of the revised definition remains unproved.

independent_acceptance_check.reason: Definition8.1(2) quantifies over arbitrary compact K+ and K-, including {x}; both images eventually lie in V, contrary to the required alternative. Condition(3) on {x,u}, u!=x, forces infinitely many distinct elements by injectivity and hence a convergent distinct-element orbit subsequence. Thus the class is empty as written. Excluding singleton sets is necessary but not a proved sufficient characterization.
